project.summary: A live conversational AI demo for GskiFlix, a fictional streaming service. This chatbot handles common support scenarios — login issues, billing disputes, playback troubleshooting, plan changes, and content discovery — with designed dialogue flows, guardrails, and escalation logic.

section.heading: Professional Context
section.body:
This demo is representative of conversation design work done on the AWS Partner Assistant, an AI-powered chatbot in the AWS Marketplace Console that helps partners navigate programs, find documentation, and troubleshoot issues.

The Partner Assistant is available to AWS Partners through the AWS Console. You can see instructions for accessing it in the AWS documentation.

Since the Partner Assistant requires AWS Console access, the demo below provides a publicly accessible example of the same conversation design principles applied to a fictional streaming service support scenario.

section.heading: The design spec behind Gski
section.body:
Gski isn't improv — it's a designed artifact. The full conversation design spec lives in Figma, laid out the way I'd hand it to a PM for sign-off: the production system prompt annotated block by block, a proposed RAG architecture for grounding answers in a real knowledge base, voice and style governance, three authored conversation flows (the money path, the guardrail path, and the happy path), and a golden response set that doubles as a regression suite.

There's also an appendix that rebuilds the entire support scope the traditional way — a left-to-right wall of ~55 hand-authored nodes covering every intent, retry, and dead end, next to the six prompt blocks that replaced it. The tooling changed; the discipline didn't.
